findings.quote: I found the last second's distance as a percent
findings.note: That is the question restated, and it is the solution's last step, not step 1 (find the total fall time from h = half g t squared). It also names nothing that separates: mistakes[1]'s student did exactly this too - found the last second's distance as a percentage - and only used the wrong denominator, so a truthful wrong-answer student could tap the right route.
findings.fix: I found the total fall time from the height

solution_defect: The option-3 entry glosses its own algebra loosely: using (n+1) squared only in the denominator gives 25%, but the gloss 'as if the fall lasted one second longer' would, applied throughout, give about 31%, not 25%. The routes author followed the entry's own wording, so this is the entry's defect, not theirs.
notes: Checked: t = 5 s, S5 = 45 m, 45/125 = 36%. The option-1 entry's 25 - 16 = 9 reproduces and calculation is a fair type (the difference-of-distances route was right, half g was dropped). The option-3 entry's 9/36 = 25% reproduces and application fits (right fraction, wrong denominator). The option-4 distractor flag is honest: 80/125 = 64% and 50/125 = 40%, and nothing I tried lands on 49%.
